    bin/collect.sh      the entry point
    lib/naming.sh       next_name: choose a free destination name
    lib/manifest.sh     manifest_has / manifest_names / manifest_name_for_hash / manifest_add

    t/test_manifest.sh  unit tests for lib/manifest.sh      <- currently FAILING
    t/run_all.sh        runs both and prints ALL TESTS PASS <- currently FAILING
    incoming/           the tree to archive
    archive/            the destination, with manifest.tsv already holding rows from earlier runs

FIRST: run `bash t/run_all.sh`. The three files under t/ are the authority on how next_name and the
manifest lookups must behave, including the cases the current code gets wrong. Read them, and read
their failure output. You MUST NOT edit, move or delete anything under t/ — the three files are
checked byte for byte afterwards. Make them pass by fixing lib/naming.sh and lib/manifest.sh.

THE MANIFEST, archive/manifest.tsv, has four TAB-separated columns: the source path relative to
incoming/, the archive name, the size in bytes, and the sha256 of the content. It is append-only:
existing rows are never rewritten or reordered.

THEN make bin/collect.sh, at that same path and still executable, run with NO arguments and do
exactly this:

 1. If incoming/ does not exist, print `error: no such directory: incoming` to stderr and exit 2.
 2. Create archive/ if needed. Consider every REGULAR FILE whose name ends in `.log` at any depth
    under incoming/, and process them in byte-wise (LC_ALL=C) ascending order of their full path,
    so the outcome is deterministic. Files not ending in `.log` are never touched, and directories
    are never removed.
 3. ALREADY RECORDED: if the file's path relative to incoming/ already appears in column 1, an
    earlier run dealt with it. SKIP it, leave it exactly where it is, and count it in `skipped`.
 4. ALREADY ARCHIVED BY CONTENT: otherwise, if the file's sha256 already appears in column 4 — from
    an earlier run OR from a row this run appended a moment ago — those bytes are in the archive
    already. Do NOT move it and do NOT make a second copy: leave it in incoming/, count it in
    `deduped`, and append a row whose column 2 is a literal `=` followed by the archive name that
    manifest_name_for_hash gives for that sha256.
 5. Otherwise MOVE it into archive/ under the name next_name gives, where the set of already-claimed
    names is the union of: every name currently present directly inside archive/, every column-2
    value in the manifest that does NOT begin with `=`, and every name this run has already
    claimed. Append its row and count it in `moved`.
 6. Rows are appended with manifest_add in processing order. No file may be overwritten or lost, and
    file contents must be unchanged by the move.
 7. Print exactly three lines to stdout and exit 0:
        moved: N
        skipped: M
        deduped: D
 8. Running it again immediately must do nothing: `moved: 0`, `deduped: 0`, and a byte-identical
    manifest. (`skipped` will be larger the second time, because rule 3 then catches the files
    rule 4 recorded.)

AND ONE MORE MODE. `bin/collect.sh --verify` changes NOTHING on disk. It reads the manifest,
IGNORING every row whose column 2 begins with `=`, and reports the remaining rows whose archive file
is not there any more, or whose file's size in bytes differs from the size the row recorded, one
line per bad row on stdout:

        missing: <archive name>
        size: <archive name> <recorded size> <actual size>

sorted by archive name byte-wise ascending under LC_ALL=C. It exits 1 when it printed at least one
line and 0 when the manifest is clean. With no manifest file at all it prints nothing and exits 0.
Any other argument is an error: `unknown option: <arg>` on stderr, exit 2.

Names in this tree contain spaces and non-ASCII bytes; no name contains a TAB or a newline. Nothing
may be word-split or globbed. Do not create a differently named script: bin/collect.sh is the entry
point. Do not delete incoming/, and do not change the contents of any file inside it.

Run `bash t/run_all.sh` and `./bin/collect.sh` yourself and read their output before you finish.

files.bin/collect.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bin/collect.sh -- archive every *.log out of incoming/.
# KNOWN BROKEN: word-splits names, ignores the manifest, clobbers duplicates.
set -u
. lib/naming.sh
. lib/manifest.sh

mkdir -p archive
declare -A TAKEN
moved=0
for f in $(find incoming -name '*.log'); do
  b=$(basename $f)
  n=$(next_name $b)
  mv $f archive/$n
  moved=$((moved + 1))
done
echo "moved: $moved"
files.lib/naming.sh:
# lib/naming.sh -- pick a free destination name in archive/.
# next_name BASENAME  prints the name to use. The caller keeps the set of names
# that are already claimed in the associative array TAKEN (the keys are names).
# KNOWN BROKEN: t/test_naming.sh does not pass.

next_name() {
  local base=$1 stem ext n cand
  case "$base" in
    *.*) stem=${base%.*}; ext=".${base##*.}" ;;
    *)   stem=$base; ext= ;;
  esac
  cand=$base
  n=1
  while [ -n "${TAKEN[$cand]+x}" ]; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    cand="$stem-$n$ext"
  done
  printf '%s' "$cand"
}
files.lib/manifest.sh:
# lib/manifest.sh -- the archive's append-only record.
# Four TAB-separated columns: source path relative to incoming/, archive name, size in bytes,
# and the sha256 of the content.
# KNOWN BROKEN: t/test_manifest.sh does not pass.

MANIFEST=archive/manifest.tsv

manifest_has() {                 # 0 when this source path was already recorded
  local want=$1
  [ -f "$MANIFEST" ] || return 1
  cut -f1 "$MANIFEST" | grep -qx "$want"
}

manifest_names() {               # every archive name ever recorded, one per line, in file order
  [ -f "$MANIFEST" ] || return 0
  cut -f2 "$MANIFEST"
}

manifest_name_for_hash() {       # print the archive name of the FIRST row with this sha256,
  local want=$1                  # and return 1 when no row has it
  [ -f "$MANIFEST" ] || return 1
  awk -F'\t' '$4 == want { print $2; exit }' "$MANIFEST"
}

manifest_add() {                 # manifest_add SOURCE_REL ARCHIVE_NAME SIZE SHA256
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" >> "$MANIFEST"
}
files.t/test_naming.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rules for next_name. Do not edit this file.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
. lib/naming.sh
fails=0
chk() {                          # chk EXPECTED BASENAME [ALREADY_TAKEN...]
  local exp=$1 base=$2 t got
  shift 2
  unset TAKEN; declare -gA TAKEN=()
  for t in "$@"; do TAKEN[$t]=1; done
  got=$(next_name "$base")
  if [ "$got" = "$exp" ]; then
    printf 'ok   next_name %-10s -> %s\n' "$base" "$got"
  else
    printf 'FAIL next_name %-10s -> %s (want %s)\n' "$base" "$got" "$exp"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}
chk 'x.log'     'x.log'
chk 'app-2.log' 'app.log'  'app.log'
chk 'app-3.log' 'app.log'  'app.log' 'app-2.log'
chk 'app.log'   'app.log'  'app-2.log'
chk 'notes-2'   'notes'    'notes'
chk 'a.b-2.c'   'a.b.c'    'a.b.c'
chk '.x-2.log'  '.x.log'   '.x.log'
chk '.hidden-2' '.hidden'  '.hidden'
chk '.hidden-3' '.hidden'  '.hidden' '.hidden-2'
printf '%d failure(s)\n' "$fails"
[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rules for the manifest lookups. Do not edit this file.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
. lib/manifest.sh
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
MANIFEST=$tmp/m.tsv
printf 'svc/dup.log\tdup.log\t5\taaaa\n'       >  "$MANIFEST"
printf 'a b/re[ad].log\tre[ad].log\t7\tbbbb\n' >> "$MANIFEST"
printf 'old/again.log\tlater.log\t5\taaaa\n'   >> "$MANIFEST"
fails=0
t() {
  if eval "$2"; then printf 'ok   %s\n' "$1"
  else printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$1"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
}
t 'exact source hit'        'manifest_has "svc/dup.log"'
t 'a dot is not a wildcard' '! manifest_has "svc/dupXlog"'
t 'brackets are literal'    'manifest_has "a b/re[ad].log"'
t 'no bracket expansion'    '! manifest_has "a b/red.log"'
t 'absent source'           '! manifest_has "nope.log"'
t 'names in file order'     '[ "$(manifest_names | tr "\n" ",")" = "dup.log,re[ad].log,later.log," ]'
t 'hash lookup'             '[ "$(manifest_name_for_hash bbbb)" = "re[ad].log" ]'
t 'first row wins'          '[ "$(manifest_name_for_hash aaaa)" = "dup.log" ]'
t 'hash miss is empty'      '[ -z "$(manifest_name_for_hash cccc)" ]'
t 'hash miss returns 1'     '! manifest_name_for_hash cccc'
printf '%d failure(s)\n' "$fails"
[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]
